items.quote: The original reference electrode material, as well as the contaminated material (with the blue layer), was analyzed by XRD (Figure 2).

items.label: working electrodes
items.quote: The working electrodes were then prepared by mixing the powders with CrF2 powder (97 pct pure; supplied by SigmaAldrich) in a weight ratio of 4:1. The prepared mixtures were pressed into discs with a diameter of 16 mm and a thickness of 3 mm (3 to 4 g). The prepared discs were placed in boron nitride crucibles and dried under vacuum (1.0 Pa) at 423 K for 12 hours. The discs were thereafter sintered in an atmosphere of argon at 1173 K for 4 hours before being mounted in the galvanic cell.
items.synthesis: The working electrodes were then prepared by mixing the powders with CrF2 powder (97 pct pure; supplied by SigmaAldrich) in a weight ratio of 4:1. The prepared mixtures were pressed into discs with a diameter of 16 mm and a thickness of 3 mm (3 to 4 g). The prepared discs were placed in boron nitride crucibles and dried under vacuum (1.0 Pa) at 423 K for 12 hours. The discs were thereafter sintered in an atmosphere of argon at 1173 K for 4 hours before being mounted in the galvanic cell.

items.label: electrolytes
items.quote: Calcium fluoride single crystals (Alfa Aesar, optical disk, 22 mm in diameter and 4 mm in thickness, polished both sides) were used as the electrolytes.
items.starting_materials: Calcium fluoride single crystals (Alfa Aesar, optical disk, 22 mm in diameter and 4 mm in thickness, polished both sides)

items.label: two-phase Cr3C2-C alloys
items.quote: Chromium carbide (Cr3C2) powder (99.5 pct pure;  325 mesh; supplied by Alfa Aesar, Germany) and graphite (99.999 pct pure; supplied by Sigma-Aldrich, Sweden) were used to prepare the two-phase Cr3C2-C alloys. The amount of carbon in the Cr-C alloy was adjusted to 18.0 wt pct. The weighed mixtures were compacted into an alumina crucible and sintered in an atmosphere of purified argon at 1273 K for 3 days under a stream of purified argon.

items.label: reference electrodes
items.quote: The reference electrodes were prepared in a similar manner; i.e., chromium powder (99.95 pct pure; supplied by Alfa Aesar) was mixed with CrF2 powder in a mass ratio of 4:1 to prepare the reference electrode.
items.starting_materials: chromium powder (99.95 pct pure; supplied by Alfa Aesar) was mixed with CrF2 powder
items.synthesis: The reference electrodes were prepared in a similar manner; i.e., chromium powder (99.95 pct pure; supplied by Alfa Aesar) was mixed with CrF2 powder in a mass ratio of 4:1 to prepare the reference electrode.

items.quote: The discs were thereafter sintered in an atmosphere of argon at 1173 K for 4 hours before being mounted in the galvanic cell.
The prepared discs were placed in boron nitride crucibles and dried under vacuum (1.0 Pa) at 423 K for 12 hours.

The weighed mixtures were compacted into an alumina crucible and sintered in an atmosphere of purified argon at 1273 K for 3 days under a stream of purified argon. (The argon purification system is described in detail in Section C.) The prepared alloys were cooled in the furnace, crushed, and ground to powders before being examined by X-ray diffraction (XRD).

items.purpose: ensure the removal of any moisture absorbed in the reaction tube or in the electrodes
items.quote: After the cell was mounted inside the reaction tube, the furnace was heated to 393 K, at a pressure of 1.0 Pa, to ensure the removal of any moisture absorbed in the reaction tube or in the electrodes. The furnace was kept at this temperature for 12 hours before being flushed with purified argon gas 3 times.
